absent: Master clock update path and kvmclock offset management outside sampling.
Behavior of timer cleanup and pending-mark helpers and reference counter source.
SynIC interrupt injection outcome mapping and LAPIC interaction details.
Memslot creation, generation bump protocol, and non-default address-space handling.
Cached guest write path and cross-slot validation beyond the read path shown.
Hypercall, reference-TSC, reenlightenment, invariant-TSC and debug MSR effects beyond partition-wide classification.
Publication and invalidation protocol for the computed TSC reference page.
Wall-clock and TSC frequency discovery and CPU hotplug effects on per-CPU rates.

findings.text: Guest clock query for a VM returns a nanosecond count by sampling internal clock state into a staging record and exposing its computed clock member.
Clock sampling repeats until the per-VM arch sequence snapshot is stable, so master state and offsets observed together form one coherent sample.

When master clock use is enabled and host TSC is deemed usable via architectural stability or a per-CPU rate, the result derives from host TSC scaled through a synthetic time record seeded from master cycle and kernel time plus offset; otherwise it derives from a boot-relative base plus offset.

Wall time plus TSC readout is only trusted when both the cached global mode and the freshly sampled mode indicate a TSC-derived source; success records realtime and host TSC indications, otherwise only a raw TSC sample is kept while stable indication remains.
Frequency conversion selects a shift and multiplier pair that keeps base and scaled rates within narrow bounds by repeated halving or doubling before a fractional division.

Realtime assembly snapshots wall seconds and cycle base under a global sequence guard, adds scaled elapsed cycles from the TSC helper, then folds the total into seconds and nanoseconds and reports the observed clock mode.

TSC delta helper distinguishes a hypervisor shared-page source, a direct hardware source, and an unsupported source; valid paths mask the cycle delta and scale it, while invalid or unsupported paths report absence and yield zero timestamp and delta.
Raw TSC read never goes backward relative to the last globally observed cycle value.

VM clock reads use a per-VM sequence counter retried on change, global wall data uses its own sequence counter with the same retry discipline, sampling pins the calling CPU for the master-path computation, and SynIC activation publishes its active flag with an ordered store.
Timer callback for a synthetic timer marks that timer pending and requests no automatic restart.
Deadline addition saturates at the maximum representable time when the requested delta in 100ns units would overflow.

Timer start separates periodic and single-shot behavior: periodic timers advance expiry forward by whole counts when behind and otherwise schedule one count ahead, while single-shot timers expire immediately when the count lies in the past and otherwise schedule at that count.

Configuration and count updates are rejected when SynIC is inactive except for host requests with zero value; guest direct-mode requests are gated on CPUID enforcement, legacy routing to SINT zero clears enable, count zero disables, and auto-enable can enable on nonzero guest counts.

Timer delivery tracks a pending flag: expiry attempts message or direct notification, clears pending and for single-shot disables on success, and the processing loop re-arms only when enabled with nonzero count and no undelivered message, otherwise releasing resources.

Message delivery requires the message page to be enabled, then inspects the target slot type: an empty slot receives a header plus payload-sized write followed by interrupt injection, an occupied slot either drops under no-retry or sets a pending indication and asks for retry.

Guest page access resolves the frame through the vCPU address-space memslot set, reusing a per-vCPU cached slot only while its generation matches the current set generation and otherwise falling back to a full search.

Cached guest access validates length against the cached extent, refreshes the cache when memslot generation changed, rejects error addresses, and uses a slow path when the region spans pages or slots.

SynIC activation initializes per-vCPU hypervisor state, publishes active state, records page-preservation choice, and enables control; assist-page access requires both VP-assist enable and EOI MSR enable before reading the cached page.
A defined set of hypervisor MSRs is treated as partition-wide, and crash notification state consists of a masked control word plus an indexed parameter array with bounds-checked access.

Reference TSC page parameters are produced only when the source clock advertises stability and the multiplier stays below an overflow threshold derived from the shift; scale then derives from shift and multiplier with centisecond normalization and offset derives from system time adjusted by timestamp times scale.

Clock exchange uses a record carrying flags, realtime, host TSC and computed clock; time records carry timestamps, system time, shift, multiplier and stability indication; timer messages carry expiration and delivery stamps; message pages are indexed by SINT with header type, flags and payload size governing delivery.

Faults surface as negative status for disabled pages, unreadable mappings, oversized intra-page ranges and failed interrupt state, while slot contention signals retry and periodic delivery suppresses retry to avoid tick pile-up.

Clock facts include realtime, host TSC and stable indications; clock mode facts include TSC, hypervisor clock and none; direct timer delivery uses fixed delivery; SynIC facts include message-page enable, VP-assist enable, EOI MSR enable and control enable; timer callback reports no restart.
